transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-05-06 14:00 UTC | Duration: ~58 minutes | Attendees: Alex Murphy, Priya Shah (Redwood); Ethan Cole, Maya Lin, Jordan Reyes, Samir Patel (Cygnus)

[00:00] Alex Murphy: Hey everyone, thanks for joining — I'm Alex from Redwood, AE on this account. Priya and I will run through scoping for the POC: quality gates, workloads, and timeline.
[00:15] Ethan Cole: Hey Alex, thanks. We'll try to keep this tight — we have a lot of internal SLAs. Quick context: Cygnus uses an LLM for doc summarization + automated triage in our support flow. Main pain is hallucination and inconsistent JSON outputs for downstream parsers.
[00:30] Priya Shah: Got it. So two main buckets: factual accuracy/hallucination rate, and structural output validation. We'll also size workload to get realistic latency/cost numbers.
[00:45] Maya Lin: For success criteria: we want <3% hallucination on golden prompts, and at least 95% schema-valid responses for JSON outputs. Latencywise p90 ideally under 1.8s for single requests, but we'll be pragmatic.
[01:03] Alex Murphy: Great, that's clear. We'll propose a set of quality gates for the POC: hallucination rate threshold, format validation pass rate, regression score delta threshold vs baseline, and operational SLOs (latency p50/p90 & error rate).
[01:20] Jordan Reyes: Can you explain how Redwood will measure hallucination? We've had different definitions internally.
[01:28] Priya Shah: Sure — practical approach: provide a golden set of prompts with human-annotated ground-truth answers (we'll call these golden prompts). During evaluation, compare model output to ground truth using a hybrid metric: exact-key matching for structured fields, plus a factuality checker that flags invented entities. For the POC we'll do a manual adjudication sample of 200 responses to calibrate the automatic checker.
[01:50] Ethan Cole: Manual adjudication is fine, but we need to minimize manual work. How many golden prompts do you need?
[01:57] Alex Murphy: For a representative POC: 500 golden prompts across high/med/low complexity. If you can supply 300 initially, we'll run a quick pass and ask for another tranche.
[02:10] Maya Lin: We can do 500, but might need guidance on splitting intents.
[02:16] Priya Shah: We'll send a template (JSONL) that includes: prompt_text, expected_json, intent_label, complexity_tag. Use the golden-prompts template Alex mentioned in next steps.
[02:28] Samir Patel: On workload sizing — our production median request is ~350 tokens and tail up to 1.2k. Concurrency peaks at 45 qps during business hours.
[02:38] Priya Shah: Helpful. For benchmarking we'll run two main profiles: latency profile (single-request p50/p90/p99 at target seq lengths: 350, 700, 1200 tokens) and throughput profile for batch loads to simulate 45 qps sustained for 10 minutes. We'll recommend Dedicated sizing after initial bench.
[02:58] Jordan Reyes: What about caching? We do have some repeat queries.
[03:02] Priya Shah: Redwood supports prefix/KV caching; we'll show estimated cost reductions. For the POC we'll instrument cache-hit metrics in the Console. Note: caching affects hallucination checks if stateful prompts are used — we'll account for that.
[03:20] Ethan Cole: On metrics, what scoring approach do you use for the regression tests?
[03:25] Priya Shah: Regression playlist will be a set of historic prompts with previous model outputs. We score against golden ground truth when available. Metrics: exact-match for strict fields, token-level F1 for free-text fields, and a composite quality score normalized 0–100. We'll flag regressions when composite drops by >3 points vs baseline.
[03:50] Maya Lin: Baseline — is that our current model? We're using an open checkpoint in prod.
[03:53] Alex Murphy: We can use your current deployment as baseline — please export a sample set. If you don't want to expose prod, a sanitized snapshot works.
[04:05] Priya Shah: Also we include format validation tests: JSON schema validation, required-key checks, enum constraints. Any failed schema check counts as a format failure and is included in the quality gate.
[04:20] Samir Patel: What's the acceptable fail rate for format until we call it failed?
[04:24] Alex Murphy: Typically for structured outputs customers want >98% pass rate on formatting. You requested 95% earlier; we can set the POC gate at 95% with a target of 98% for go/no-go.
[04:38] Ethan Cole: Sounds reasonable. Now on hallucination detection: can Redwood run an automatic entity-checker or do we need to label?
[04:45] Priya Shah: We'll run an initial automated factuality pass using an entity overlap + knowledge-distinctness heuristic. But best practice is hybrid: automated tagging plus the manual adjudication sample. That manual sample trains a lightweight classifier to reduce future labeling.
[05:02] Maya Lin: OK. How long for the evaluation runs? We want the POC to be time-boxed.
[05:07] Alex Murphy: Proposed timeline: Week 0 (this week) — align and collect artifacts. Week 1 — ingest golden prompts and initial benchmarks (1M tokens run). Week 2 — run full regression playlist + manual adjudication sample, refine scoring. Week 3 — present results, iterate on prompt engineering and quantization/ops knobs. Week 4 — final review and go/no-go. So a 4-week POC.
[05:30] Jordan Reyes: Can you do the initial 1M-token benchmark on Dedicated? We want realistic costs.
[05:35] Priya Shah: Yes, we'll run the 1M-token benchmark on a Dedicated medium config (we recommend 2xA100-equivalent or patched config), and also run a Private VPC smoke test for networking latencies. We'll provide a cost model: cost per 1M tokens, and projected monthly cost at your 45 qps peak.
[05:55] Ethan Cole: On security/compliance: we need SOC2 reports and KMS/HSM support for Private — can you surface those in the POC?
[06:03] Alex Murphy: Yes, we'll share SOC2, ISO summary, and KMS integration docs. For Private deployments we can show an on-prem packaging checklist; Jordan, we'll need your network diagram per action item.
[06:20] Maya Lin: Good. For scoring thresholds, propose we use the following gates: hallucination <=3% (manual sample calibrated), format pass >=95%, composite quality >=85, latency p90 <=2.0s for 350-token median. If any two gates fail, default to remediation; if three fail, POC failed.
[06:46] Priya Shah: That sounds practical. We'll also add a regression gate: no new regression with composite score drop >3 points.
[06:54] Samir Patel: For the regression playlist size — how many historical items do you need?
[06:58] Priya Shah: Recommend minimum 2k items representative of intents. If you can deliver 2k tagged by intent that helps; at minimum 500 for early pass.
[07:10] Ethan Cole: We'll target 2k, but may ship 1k first.
[07:15] Alex Murphy: Fine. We'll scope the evaluation harness to accept streaming outputs and also support tool-calls / function calling traces if needed. Might matter for your parser.
[07:27] Maya Lin: Our downstream pipeline relies on strict JSON in the 'response' field — if the model emits extraneous text we break.
[07:33] Priya Shah: We'll run forced-formatting techniques and a post-processor that validates and repairs minor JSON issues. We'll treat repaired outputs as partially successful with a lower score.
[07:46] Jordan Reyes: How will you present results? Dashboard/export?
[07:50] Alex Murphy: The Redwood Console will show per-route dashboards: pass/fail counts, hallucination rates, latency histograms, and downloadable CSV/JSON reports. Priya will deliver an evaluation summary deck at the end of Week 2 and a final report Week 4.
[08:05] Ethan Cole: Great. A few edge-case asks: 1) We need to test hallucination on PII fields — ensure model doesn't invent email addresses. 2) We want a small adversarial test set for hallucination stress.
[08:16] Priya Shah: We'll include a 200-item adversarial set focusing on PII and entity hallucination. We'll mark these as high-priority for manual review.
[08:25] Maya Lin: Cost target — we want to understand unit economics. Can Redwood provide a per-route cost estimate with caching and batching knobs enabled?
[08:33] Alex Murphy: Yes, we'll produce a cost sensitivity table: per-token cost across quantization profiles, with caching applied at 10/30/50% hit rates. That will be in Priya's benchmark spreadsheet.
[08:47] Samir Patel: On infra: if we go Dedicated, what's the recommended autoscale/burst config?
[08:52] Priya Shah: For your 45 qps peak and median sizes, recommend steady Dedicated pool sized for ~70% utilization and a burst pool for spikes. We'll propose autoscale thresholds and a failover to hosted tier for very high bursts.
[09:06] Ethan Cole: Failover to hosted is risky for data residency — we need opt-in.
[09:09] Alex Murphy: Understood, will make sure policies are explicit and opt-in.
[09:15] Maya Lin: Any blockers you foresee for starting Week 1?
[09:18] Priya Shah: Only artifact collection: golden prompts, regression playlist export, and network diagram. If we get those, we can run Week 1 benchmarks.
[09:26] Ethan Cole: We'll start exporting — Samir will coordinate.
[09:30] Jordan Reyes: One more: can the evaluation harness include format fuzz tests? Like missing brackets and different ordering?
[09:36] Priya Shah: Yes, we'll include schema fuzzing — randomizing order and injecting whitespace/noise to test parser robustness. Results will be broken out separately.
[09:46] Alex Murphy: Quick recap and next steps: Alex sends golden-prompts JSONL template + pricing matrix; Priya builds bench harness and runs 1M-token Dedicated run; Cygnus sends 500–2k golden prompts and 1–2k regression items; Jordan sends network/VPC diagram. We'll reconvene with preliminary results in one week and a full deck in two weeks.
[10:10] Maya Lin: Thanks everyone. Quick note: share the SOC2 + KMS docs to our security alias.
[10:16] Alex Murphy: Will do. Closing notes: I'll add calendar invite for POC kickoff week of May 25.
[10:24] (meeting ends)

Notes: transcription contains occasional mis-heard words (e.g., "KV cash" instead of "KV cache"), speaker overlap at ~07:30. Shared artifacts referenced: [link] Redwood golden-prompts template (drive.redwood/golden-prompts.jsonl), [link] Priya benchmark spreadsheet (drive.redwood/bench-cygnus-2026-05), SOC2 summary (redwood.com/soc2.pdf).
